intro.value: A family-run campsite and RV park tucked among tall trees in the centre of Selfoss, the largest town in South Iceland. It is open all year, needs no booking for individual travellers, and has a heated service centre with a kitchen, a big dining room and hot showers, plus 40 electric hook-up pitches and a chemical toilet disposal point.

season.value: Open all year round (campsite and RV park); no pre-booking for individuals, groups should email ahead

winter.value: Open all year. The service centre (reception, kitchen, showers) is open until 20:00 in winter and 22:00 in summer; if you arrive after closing you can set up and register and pay the next morning.

electricity.value: Yes – electric hook-ups on 40 pitches in the separate RV area (1,900 ISK/night)

kitchen.value: Yes – indoor kitchen and a big dining room in the service centre

showers.value: Yes – hot showers in the service centre, with no separate shower charge listed in the 2026 prices. The geothermal hot water smells slightly of sulphur.

toilets.value: Yes – WC in the service centre

laundry.value: Washing machine, tumble dryer and shoe dryer on site (small fee)

camping_card.value: No – Selfoss/Gesthús is not among the campsites in the Útilegukortið (Camping Card) 2026 list.

dump_station.value: Yes – chemical disposal point for motorhome/cassette toilets, plus drinking-water fill; tjalda.is also lists emptying of water tanks

practical.value: No reservations needed for individuals. Register and pay at the service centre before setting up; if staff have to collect payment at your pitch, an extra service fee applies.
Arriving after the service centre closes is fine: set up and pay the next morning. Check-out from the campsite and RV park is before 12:00.
Quiet hours are 00:00–07:00, with no unnecessary vehicle traffic in that window. Open fires are not allowed.
Breakfast is sold in the service centre 08:00–10:00 every day, along with coffee, soft drinks, beer and wine.
About 5 minutes' walk to the swimming pool and a large playground, and about 10 minutes to the town centre with supermarkets, restaurants and the post office.
Tents and motorhomes/folding campers use two separate areas; the electric pitches are in the RV area.
Tap water is drinkable: let the cold tap run a moment so it isn't mixed with the sulphur-scented geothermal hot water.
